newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's BNDES to begin water, sewage co sell-offs.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's BNDES to begin water, sewage co sell-offs.

text.p: Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) is due to start working on a first privatization of a state-level water and sewage company, the bank's president said.

In an interview with newspaper O Estado de Sao Paulo, Luiz Carlos Mendonca de Barros said the BNDES would begin next week drawing up a plan for the privatization of Espirito Santo state's water and sewage company, Sesan.
"Next week we will announce the first operation to encourage privatization of water and sewage, opening up a new front in the privatization program," Mendonca de Barros said.
The BNDES president also told the newspaper he expected the privatization of four big electricty generators owned by federal power holding Eletrobras to start in 1998.
Sale of the first company likely to be sold, Furnas, should raise between six and eight billion reais, he said.
Mendonca de Barros said differences remained within the government as to how revenues from the upcoming privatization of Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) should be used.
The BNDES president said he backed proposals drawn up in the Senate that some of the expected six billion reais raised in next year's privatization to be invested in regional infrastructure projects.

But, given the insistence by the government's economic team that the receipts be used for reducing Brazil's debt stockpile, any final decision may have to be taken by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, Mendonca de Barros said.
